raw_response:
I've been working this land since I was a teenager. My father grew wheat and corn, his father grew wheat and corn. This land in Quzhou is flat North China Plain — good for nothing else really. My legs aren't what they were, so I can't do much hand labor anymore. My son helps during harvest but lives in the city now.

I have about 10 mu. I'll keep 8 mu in the wheat-corn rotation like always — plant wheat in October, harvest it in June, turn around and put corn in right after. The other 2 mu behind the house I'll put some vegetables in spring, mostly for us to eat, maybe sell a little.

For wheat, I'll use the Jimai variety the county extension station recommended a few years back — not the old stuff, but not the newest either, I know it works on my soil. Four waterings: one when I sow it, one before it freezes, one at jointing, one when the grain is filling. I'll put compound fertilizer down at planting, then urea at jointing. Two sprays — one for the aphids in May, one for powdery mildew.

For maize, I'll buy hybrid seed from the cooperative, same as last year — Xianyu 335. I'll direct seed it right after the wheat combine goes through, no need to plow again. Only water once unless the summer is really dry. One pesticide spray for corn borer if I see them bad.

I'm not changing much. At 70, I know what this land gives me if I treat it right.
